title: The honest experiment readout
promise: Turn the raw numbers of an A/B test into a ship, extend or stop decision, with the checks that catch a broken test before it fools you.
gives: A one-page readout: the verdict, the checks behind it, the effect with its interval, and what to do next.
ask: Read out the reorder card test. Should we ship?
demoNote: The agent hands the counts to a script, which checks the split before it looks at the result. When it ends, change the numbers or pick another scenario and watch the verdict move.
clipTitle: An A/B readout that *checks the test first*
clipLine: The split is tested before the result. The script does the arithmetic.

example.label: The reorder card test
example.note: A two-week test on 41,870 returning customers with three guardrails. The decision is to extend.

when: A test has finished and someone wants a yes or no.
The dashboard says significant and you want to know whether to believe it.
You have to explain a result to people who do not read statistics.
skip: You are designing a test. This reads results. It does not size an experiment in advance.
The metric is neither a rate nor a simple mean per user, such as revenue with heavy outliers. Ask an analyst.
The test is still running and you plan to stop when it looks good. That is the mistake this skill exists to flag.

inputs.name: The planned split and duration
inputs.note: For example 50/50 for 14 days. Needed for the sample ratio check.

inputs.name: Guardrail metrics
inputs.note: The things that must not get worse, with their counts.

inputs.name: The smallest effect worth shipping
inputs.note: If you did not set one before the test, say so.

outputs.name: readout.html
outputs.note: The verdict with its reasons, a chart of the effect and its interval, and the guardrails.

outputs.name: readout.json
outputs.note: Every computed number, so the result can be reproduced.

steps.title: Check the test before the result
steps.body: A script tests the sample ratio first. If users were not split as planned, the readout stops there.

steps.title: Compute, do not estimate
steps.body: The script calculates the difference, its confidence interval and the p-value. The model never does the arithmetic.

steps.title: Ask whether the test could have seen it
steps.body: It works out the smallest effect the test had the power to detect and sets it beside the effect you care about.

steps.title: Read the guardrails
steps.body: Each one is computed the same way and marked held, worse or unclear.

steps.title: Look for the usual traps
steps.body: Stopped early, too short to cover a weekly cycle, or many metrics tested with no correction.

steps.title: Give one verdict
steps.body: Ship, extend, stop or do not trust, with the two or three facts that decide it.

checks.name: The numbers were computed, not written
checks.note: The checker reruns the statistics on the counts stored in the file and compares every figure.

checks.name: The split was checked before the result
checks.note: A chi-square test on the sample ratio. Below p = 0.001 the only decision allowed is do not trust.

checks.name: The verdict follows the fixed rule
checks.note: Eight rules, first match wins. The decision is code, and the headline has to open with it.

checks.name: Every figure in the prose is in the numbers
checks.note: A number in the headline, summary or next steps that the script did not compute fails.

checks.name: Guardrails that did not hold are named
checks.note: A guardrail that is worse or unclear has to appear by name in the summary.

checks.name: Early stopping is called out
checks.note: A test that stopped early or ran a part week has to say so.

checks.name: The counts are the right counts
checks.note: Know where the numbers came from before you paste them in.

failures.title: Right arithmetic on wrong data
failures.body: If the counts include bots, double-counted users or a tracking bug, the readout will be precise and wrong.
failures.catch: The sample ratio check catches many of these, not all. Ask where the counts came from.

failures.title: A guardrail counted per order
failures.body: The test changes who orders. The share of large orders can fall because new, smaller orders were added, with no existing basket getting smaller.
failures.catch: The skill tells the agent to say so. Look at the full spread before you call it harm.

failures.title: One kind of test
failures.body: Two arms, a rate per user, read once at the planned end. More arms, revenue per user and tests that were watched daily need another method.
failures.catch: The skill stops and says what kind of analysis it needs.

failures.title: Significant is not the same as important
failures.body: A real effect can be too small to matter.
failures.catch: The script flags an interval that reaches below the smallest effect you said was worth shipping. Set that number before the test.

run.by: A fresh agent session, given only the skill folder and the counts written the way a product manager would paste them. Nobody answered its questions.
run.note: Run twice. Both passed on the first run of the checker. The first run found that a win whose interval dips below the agreed minimum effect went unremarked, so the script now flags it. The readout shown here is from the second run, unedited.
